Thanks for the heads-up. I reproduced a local perf test against psi9-v2.4 on a canary host configured similarly to Sentinel's Dedicated pool. Observations:

- v2.4 introduces a new fused attention kernel that benefits short tokens but regresses on >1k context with current CUDA 12.3 driver builds we observed in us-west-2.
- KV cache eviction pattern changed subtly; this increases memory churn and causes a handful of extra memcpy ops before token emission in our runtime.
- Rebuilding the runtime with the legacy attention fallback for v2.4 removes the regression in our tests.

Mitigation options (pros/cons):
1) Traffic pin to psi9-v2.3-compatible binary (fast, reversible, small perf hit vs baseline).
2) Rollforward to a v2.4 runtime built with legacy-attn path (requires a rebuild + CI smoke, ~3–5 hours to validate and patch canary, ~6–8 hours full rollout).
3) Temporary traffic split to a verified variant with quantization-profile that avoids fused kernel (works but needs config and may change output distribution).

Given Sentinel's production impact, option 1 is quickest. If leadership approves, I can do the pin within 30 minutes and then push the v2.4 legacy-attn runtime as a follow-up (option 2) to restore traffic to the nominal variant.

I will attach the basic perf logs to INF-9832.

-Rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
